answer: Picture a gym where one turnstile guards the door, with an atlas of member gyms behind the desk. Each agent holds one membership card tied to its key, photo on file, and each turnstile stamps entries by quartz clock. Peers sample the log each epoch: a card that never scans, or scans in two cities at once, loses standing. A borrowed card fails the photo check, and no card passes twice before dawn at the morning rush. Forging a thousand agents means a thousand memberships at $40 a month, $40,000 every month, plus a thousand bodies at the door.
